reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: 01e file: 01e_PARTIAL_W2B3_1771748669.json, invariant: 'Publishing data columns must only occur on subnets the node is subscribed to (custody/sampling).' Code reading is factually correct: routeSignedBeaconBlock (L161-167) loops through ALL data columns and broadcasts each to its computed subnet, while nimbus_beacon_node.nim (L1350-1352) only subscribes to custody group subnets (~8-16 of 128). However, this is a code-intrinsic deviation (Step C2 type b). The proposer's own construction logic publishes to all subnets regardless of subscription status - no external attacker controls or triggers this behavior. The proposer itself decides to broadcast all 128 columns. This is a spec-compliance issue (violates 01e requirement) but not a security vulnerability because it lacks attacker causation. It's a correctness bug in the proposer's publishing logic, not an exploitable security finding. Attacker control: none. Path type: code-intrinsic. The issue causes operational concerns (libp2p errors, failed delivery, peer reputation degradation) but does not create an attack surface. Per quality gates rule 9, code-intrinsic deviations must be DISPUTED_FP regardless of spec violation.
